title: Test safely, guard your keys, plan for failure

say: Test safely, guard your keys, and plan for failure.
This is the video for module two of API Fundamentals.

A browser address bar can only send GET requests, and it hides the headers. To test real APIs you need an API client, a tool where you pick the method, URL, headers and body, and see the full response.

say: Real API work starts with a need, such as: we want to know automatically when a customer has paid. You read the documentation, then test safely before anything goes live.

say: Postman suits saved collections and teams on a laptop.
Also learn to read curl, because most documentation shows examples that way. Dash H adds a header, dash d is the body, and dash X sets the method.
Practise on fake APIs like JSONPlaceholder, which only pretends to save. Never experiment with DELETE on a real business account.

say: Good documentation answers the same questions every time. Find the base URL, where every endpoint starts. Then how you prove who you are. Most APIs take a key in the Authorization header as a Bearer token.

say: A secret key can act on the whole account, including money. Keep it on the server only, never in app code users download. Never send it on WhatsApp or email, or paste it into AI chats, screenshots or shared documents. Keep it out of GitHub.
If a key may have leaked, generate a new one at once, which stops the old one working.

panel.heading: Treat a secret key like your bank PIN
items: Keep it on the server side only
Never on WhatsApp, email or AI chats
Never in screenshots or shared documents
Keep it out of code on GitHub
If it may have leaked, generate a new one

say: First, rate limits. A 429 means too many requests. Wait as long as the Retry-After header says. For temporary server errors, wait and double the wait each time. Never automatically retry a POST that moves money.

cards.d: Wait as long as Retry-After says. 3,600 seconds is one hour. For 5xx, back off: 1, 2, 4, 8 seconds.
230 records at 50 per page is 5 pages. Count the total against a second source.
Check the signature, reply 200 OK fast, skip repeats, verify before delivering.

say: Second, pages. Grace in Kaduna needed 230 transactions at 50 per page, so 5 pages. Had she stopped at page 1, 180 would have been missing.

say: Third, webhooks, where the provider calls your URL when something happens, such as a payment. Check the signature, reply 200 OK at once, and expect the same event more than once.
Never release goods on a screenshot or an unverified webhook. Scammers send fake alerts.

say: APIs change, keys expire, and the builder moves on. A short run sheet lets someone else keep it working. Record the business need, its owner, and the exact documentation pages.

panel.heading: The API run sheet
items: Provider, base URL and docs links
Where keys are stored, never the keys

say: List each endpoint with its units. Record where keys are stored and who can access them, but never the keys themselves.

say: To remember. Practise on fake APIs and in test mode. Verify amount and currency. Keep secret keys on the server, and replace any that leak. Respect Retry-After, and count every page.
